semantic_correction.stem: During a community meeting, a resident asks a public health nurse why the local health department supports a comprehensive syringe services program (SSP). Which response is most accurate?

options.A: They provide sterile injection equipment and safe disposal, testing and vaccination, and links to treatment while reducing infectious-disease risk without increasing drug use or crime.
options.B: They provide sterile injection equipment as a substitute for substance-use treatment, so participants generally do not need referral for treatment or other medical services.
options.C: They reduce blood-borne infection mainly by requiring participants to stop injecting drugs before sterile equipment, testing, vaccination, or referral services are provided.
options.D: They are designed mainly to identify people who inject drugs for law-enforcement referral, with sterile equipment and health services used chiefly to support that process.

semantic_correction.rationale: CDC describes syringe services programs as community-based prevention programs that provide access to sterile syringes and injection equipment, safe disposal, infectious-disease testing and vaccination, and linkage to infectious-disease care and substance-use treatment. CDC also states that comprehensive SSPs are safe and effective, reduce transmission risk for HIV, hepatitis C, viral hepatitis, and other infections, and do not increase illegal drug use or crime. Therefore A is the most accurate response. B is incorrect because SSPs link participants to substance-use treatment rather than replace it. C is incorrect because abstinence is not a prerequisite for receiving harm-reduction services. D mischaracterizes SSPs as law-enforcement referral programs rather than public-health prevention programs.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Explain that comprehensive syringe services programs reduce injection-related infectious-disease risk by providing sterile equipment and other prevention services while linking participants to testing, vaccination, medical care, and substance-use treatment rather than requiring abstinence or serving as law-enforcement programs.
semantic_correction.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
semantic_correction.source_document_title: Strengthening Syringe Services Programs (SSPs); Infectious Diseases in Persons Who Inject Drugs; Viral Hepatitis Among People Who Use or Inject Drugs
semantic_correction.source_version_date: Core CDC SSP pages dated February–March 2024 and live/rechecked August 20, 2026; current 2026 CDC HIV surveillance content independently continues to describe SSPs as community-based prevention programs providing sterile equipment and linkage to health services
semantic_correction.source_locator: Strengthening SSPs, ‘Syringe Service Programs Explained’: access to sterile syringes and disposal; testing and vaccination; linkage to infectious-disease and substance-use treatment; comprehensive SSPs do not increase illegal drug use or crime and reduce infectious-disease transmission. Infectious Diseases in PWID repeats the same comprehensive-services and safety/effectiveness claims. Viral Hepatitis Among People Who Use or Inject Drugs states SSPs provide sterile equipment, testing/vaccination and treatment linkage and are associated with reduced HIV/HCV incidence.
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: Comprehensive SSPs are community-based harm-reduction/prevention programs that provide sterile injection equipment and safe disposal plus testing, vaccination, and treatment linkage; CDC states they reduce infectious-disease risk and do not increase illegal drug use or crime.
semantic_correction.blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
semantic_correction.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance, printed p.9 (official PDF pageno 12): plan and/or participate in community health education; educate client about prevention and treatment of high-risk health behaviors; assess and educate clients about health risks based on family, population and community.
semantic_correction.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — community harm reduction and prevention of blood-borne infection
semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup retained the SSP public-health construct and rebuilt A/B/C/D so the correct response is not uniquely longest while preserving CDC-supported sterile-equipment, prevention-service, linkage-to-care, and safety claims.

scope_exclusions.local_legality: The item does not test whether SSP operation is authorized under a particular state or local law.
scope_exclusions.abstinence: The item does not claim that SSP participation requires continued drug use; it tests that abstinence is not a prerequisite for harm-reduction services.
scope_exclusions.effect_size: No numeric HIV or HCV incidence reduction is tested.
scope_exclusions.crime: The item uses the CDC population-level evidence statement that comprehensive SSPs do not increase illegal drug use or crime; it does not make a prediction about an individual neighborhood event.
scope_exclusions.treatment: SSPs complement and link to substance-use treatment; they are not presented as a replacement for evidence-based treatment.

near_duplicate_check.note: Targeted GitHub search for ‘syringe services program sterile injection equipment testing vaccination treatment HIV HCV crime’ returned no indexed repository match. No broad bank scan was performed.

option_audit.A: Correct. It accurately combines the core SSP services and the CDC-supported finding that comprehensive SSPs reduce infectious-disease risk without increasing illegal drug use or crime.
option_audit.B: Plausible because SSPs provide sterile equipment, but they also link participants to substance-use treatment and other health services rather than substitute for treatment.
option_audit.C: Plausible to someone who equates prevention with abstinence, but harm-reduction services are provided without making cessation of injection a prerequisite.
option_audit.D: Plausible as a misconception about public programs involving drug use, but SSPs are public-health prevention programs rather than programs designed chiefly for law-enforcement referral.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible best answer. A is the only option that accurately describes both comprehensive SSP services and their public-health role without substituting for treatment, imposing abstinence as a prerequisite, or converting the program into law-enforcement surveillance.

cueing_check.note: The key is only modestly longer than the distractors and all four options contain comparable detail and structure; the original extreme length cue is removed.

blueprint_audit.entry_level_relevance: NCSBN Health Promotion and Maintenance explicitly includes community health education, education about high-risk health behaviors, and population/community risk education; SSP teaching directly maps to these activities.
blueprint_audit.visual_verification: VERIFIED. Official 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan screenshot pageno 12 / printed p.9 was successfully retrieved August 20, 2026 and visibly shows the cited Health Promotion and Maintenance activity statements.

source_verification.note: Multiple live CDC SSP/PWID pages were rechecked August 20, 2026. Current 2026 CDC HIV surveillance content independently continues to describe SSPs as community-based prevention programs that provide sterile syringes and linkage to treatment and other prevention services.
